name: Artemisinin from crude A. annua extract, flow (Triemer 2018)
source: S. Triemer, K. Gilmore, G. T. Vu, P. H. Seeberger and A. Seidel-Morgenstern, Angew. Chem. Int. Ed., 2018, 57, 5525. Main text Fig. 4; ESI Sections 2.2, 3.2, 3.3.2 and Table S9 (NaHCO3 quench).

materials.name: O2 (5.6 NmL/min, 7 bar)
materials.note: 5.6 NmL/min / 22.414 L/mol over the 10 min needed to deliver 1 mmol DHAA

materials.name: dried A. annua leaves (extracted)
materials.note: 96 g leaves per 542 mL toluene extract (ESI 2.2) x 2.0 mL feed; source of the chlorophyll photosensitiser

energy.device: 420 nm LED module (36.3 V x 2.1 A)

notes: Feed volume taken as toluene (upper bound; dissolved DHAA and TFA occupy part of the 2.0 mL).
Native DHAA in the extract (3.11 mM) is <1% of the 0.5 M feed and is neglected; DHAA was added as a purified solid.
The -20 C cooling bath (immersion cooler) is not inventoried; its energy is not reported.
Aqueous NaHCO3 quench volume not stated; reaction-step boundary only.
